A 105-year-old survivor of the 1921 Tulsa race massacre and some victims' descendants are demanding reparations, arguing that the city's current racial and economic disparities can be traced back to the violence in what was known as Black Wall Street.

Many lawsuits demanding accountability for the massacre have come and gone, but attorneys say this one is different. It's based on Oklahoma's nuisance law, which the state recently relied on in its successful suits against opioid companies like J&J.

The lawsuit demanding reparations argues that the massacre violates public nuisance law by creating and perpetuating vast inequalities for Tulsa’s Black residents that persist to this day (unemployment, median household income, life expectancy, etc.)
